chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Amr ibn Saeed ibn Hilal who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Advise me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I advise you with the fear of Allah, and devoutness (war'), and striving (ijtihad), and know that striving would not benefit if there is no devoutness in it.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الِاجْتِهَادُ: Striving or exertion in religious duties

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between striving and devoutness in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Amr ibn Sa'id to integrate ijtihad (striving/effort) with wara' (pious caution), highlighting that religious effort is futile without moral vigilance. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on wara' as the essential safeguard that validates intellectual and practical exertion, ensuring actions are not only correct but also spiritually pure and free from doubtful matters.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Amro Bin Saeed Bin Hilal who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Advise me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> advise you with the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the devoutness, and the striving; and know that the striving would not benefit if there is no devoutness in it’.
en.sarwar: 11. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Aqaba from abu Kahmas from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id ibn Hilal who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) to instruct me with good advice. The Imam said, ‘I recommend you to be pious before Allah, restrain from worldly matters (sins) and work hard. Note that there is no benefit in hard work without restraint from worldly matters.’”
